title: a nested loop reused the outer loop's index, rewinding it over already-freed fields
object: the per-interface description strings, each a g_strdup
lifetime_ender: g_free(wtapng_if_descr->opt_comment) on the first pass over interface index i
shape: a shared loop index, so finishing the inner loop rewinds the outer one
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is the SAME free on a repeated pass, because the inner loop reset `i`.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: the construct no longer exists -- v4.6.8's wtap_close does not walk interfaces itself, it calls `wtap_block_array_free(wth->shb_hdrs)` and siblings, so neither loop survives (`grep -c 'gint i, j;'` = 0 because the whole teardown was replaced). A fix-reversal against history.
nested_why: the object came straight from g_malloc / g_new / g_new0 / g_strdup / getline -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no wmem allocator between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../wmem-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: neither free is wrong and neither bound is wrong -- the defect is that ONE variable serves two loops, so the outer cursor is rewound and the same fields are freed again. The missing `= NULL` after each free is what turns the rewind from a no-op into a second release, which is why the fix declares a second index rather than clearing any field.
